summary.one_liner: ToolGit is a collection of scripts that extend Git with extra sub-commands for everyday repository tasks such as deleting stale branches, force-pulling, and searching history.
summary.what_it_does: ToolGit provides about 16 Git sub-commands implemented as scripts named git-*, so they can be invoked as "git <command>" once the folder is on PATH. Branch commands include git-gone (delete local branches that no longer exist on the remote), git-forward (fetch and fast-forward all remote tracking branches), and git-force-pull (fetch and hard-reset to the remote tracking branch). Query commands such as git-in-repo, git-is-head-detached, git-is-worktree-clean, git-is-branch-remote, and git-main-branch return status codes or the default branch name for use in scripts. Other tools cover rebasing the whole history onto a revision (git-legacy), restoring file modes in the index or worktree (git-mode-restore), and searching history for strings only in added or removed lines (git-xlog). The README also describes git.ini-style aliases in aliases.ini for shortcuts like amend, graph, root, dir, and gc-all. Each script accepts -? for help.
use_cases: delete local branches whose remote was removed
force a branch to match its remote
restore file permissions after a chmod mess
search git history for added or removed lines containing a string
check from a script whether the working tree is clean
how_to_run: Extract ToolGit to a folder of your choice.
Add that folder to your PATH environment variable.
Optionally run: git config set --append --global include.path path/to/toolgit/aliases.ini
Run a command with -? to see its options, e.g. git mode-restore -?
notable: Git sub-commands installed simply by placing git-* scripts on PATH
Includes a mode-restore tool for fixing file permission changes in index and worktree
git-xlog searches history only in added or removed lines
Optional aliases.ini adds short git aliases
caveats: Installation is manual: extract files and edit PATH yourself
README does not describe platform support beyond Posix tarball and Windows zip downloads
Some commands like git-force-pull and git-legacy rewrite state destructively
